correctness.rationale: Orthogonal wheel Laplacian decomposition has a constant eigenvector, a hub-versus-rim eigenvector, and isolated sine/cosine rim Fourier blocks. The only collision is at \(a\mu_j=mb\); interior collisions make three-dimensional eigenspaces, antipodal collision is only two-dimensional. Restriction determinants for two rim vertices equal \(\sin(2\pi jt/m)\), yielding gcd conditions and Euler totient counts. Hub+adjacent rim samples yield a nonzero 3×3 determinant at each interior collision, while adjacent rim samples suffice otherwise. For prime rim orders any three distinct unit-circle sample points form a nonsingular affine Fourier triple, and a hub plus two rim points are also nonsingular. The standalone verifier returned VERIFY_OK 12705 checks including full assembled-matrix PBH and exact-rational Kalman ranks; these finite checks supplement, not establish, the universal proof.

value.rationale: The minimum number of independently actuated vertices jumps sharply from two to three at a discrete, exactly characterized set of conductance ratios. All optimal two-actuator locations and counts are given by arithmetic separation rules, with a nontrivial even-rim antipodal exception. At odd prime order any triple of vertices is optimal at each resonance. These are natural complete classifications directly useful to placement and sensitivity questions, not a one-parameter numerical table or a routine restatement of PBH.
